title: Understanding the TOK Exhibition
summary: A student-facing guide to the TOK Exhibition: the 35 IA prompts, choosing specific objects, the 950-word commentary, the rubric, common myths and a term timeline.
overview: A single reference page to hand students when you launch the Exhibition. It explains the components (one IA prompt, three objects, a commentary of up to 950 words), lists all 35 official IA prompts, and uses side-by-side examples to show generic and specific objects ('a stock photo of a Bible' versus 'my grandfather's 1950 Bible with his notes').

It also covers the level descriptors (0–10), the required teacher–student interactions, a set of myths and pitfalls, tips for success (including a 'triangulation' method so that each object argues something different) and a month-by-month roadmap.
questions: How does TOK show up in the objects around us?
What makes an object's link to a prompt convincing rather than descriptive?
time: An introductory lesson, then a reference for the whole term
heads_up: The roadmap, deadlines and the showcase event are for our class of May 2027. Edit the dates for your own calendar.
